It debuted in [[HZ091]], replacing [[Only One Story]]. The song is also used as the opening theme for the Asian English release of [[Pokémon Horizons: Season 3—Rising Hope]] with English subtitles, debuting in ''[[HZ092|Following Traces of Laquium]]'' and replacing [[Will (song)|Will -Korean ver.-]]. The full version of the song was released as a [[List of Pokémon digital singles#GET BACK|digital single]] on May 21, 2025. ==Opening animation== ===Synopsis=== [[Liko]], [[Roy]], [[Dot]], {{TP|Liko|Meowscarada}}, {{TP|Roy|Crocalor}}, and {{TP|Dot|Quaxwell}} step forward and watch the sunrise, with the screen suddenly switching to a film-like montage of the [[Rising Volt Tacklers]] before {{p|Floragato}}'s [[Evolution]] into Meowscarada. In a grassy field, Liko and Meowscarada look into the distance before walking away. The two are then joined by {{TP|Liko|Hattrem}} and [[Pagogo]], sitting on the stairs under the shade, watching Trainers and Pokémon. Roy, Crocalor, {{TP|Roy|Kilowattrel}}, {{TP|Roy|Lucario}}, and [[Captain Pikachu]] in a forest are shown for a brief moment, followed by Dot (who was eating a donut), Quaxwell, {{TP|Dot|Tinkatuff}}, and {{TP|Dot|Gimmighoul}} then [[Ult]] and {{p|Sableye}} on a tree, a {{i|Poké Ball}}, and finally Liko finishing getting ready as Meowscarada stretches from the bed. A series of flashback transitions occur as {{p|Sprigatito}}, Floragato, and Meowscarada appear. After tying her shoes, Liko sets off with Meowscarada, Hattrem, and Pagogo in tow. The camera pans over the characters during certain times of the day – starting with Hattrem at dawn, Meowscarada at daytime, Liko in the evening, alongside {{TP|Liko|Charcadet}}, and Pagogo at night in its {{form|Terapagos|Terastal Form}}. Liko looks up as green leaves appear when she opens her eyes. Under the green spotlight stands Liko and Meowscarada, whose flowers explode into pink petals. Liko and Meowscarada are shown battling [[Coral]], [[Sidian]], {{p|Glalie}}, and {{p|Garganacl}}. At the snap of Meowscarada's fingers, several of her flowers fall from above as Meowscarada does the same. The [[Explorers]] are shown one by one, starting with Coral, Sidian, Glalie, and Garganacl, followed by [[Chalce]] and {{p|Medicham}}, and ending with [[Spinel]] and {{p|Umbreon}}, with [[Indi]] and [[Rubina]] behind them. The sun sets at a beach, [[Amethio]] and {{TP|Amethio|Ceruledge}} watching it from ashore. The Rising Volt Tacklers' flag is back blowing in the wind after their reunion. Liko is running towards the left side of the screen, reaching out for something as the series logo appears. Roy and Cap appear right after the series logo, with the two, Crocalor, Lucario, and Kilowattrel moving along a path as Roy's [[Mega Ring]] briefly shines. In a city, Ult stares at his [[Dusk Ball]] in an alleyway before briefly glancing at camera while leaving. Cap falls into an abyss as the camera zooms out of his eye, with Cap looking confident on Roy's shoulder once the camera fully zooms out. Roy and his Pokémon team have dinner together around a campfire, unaware of the [[Black Rayquaza]] flying above them. Once again, the camera pans over the characters during certain times of the day – starting with Kilowattrel at daytime, Crocalor in the evening, Roy and Cap at night, and Lucario at dawn. Roy looks up as orange sparks appear when he opens his eyes. Under the red spotlight stands Roy and Crocalor, who shoots {{m|Flamethrower}} towards the camera. Clinking their Mega Rings, Roy and Ult stand back to back as their Mega Pokémon battle on the ground. In the air, Kilowattrel and Crocalor attack with {{m|Electro Ball}} and Flamethrower. Mega Lucario shows up behind them and attacks the ground. On a Rotom Phone, Roy and Crocalor dance, Ult and Sableye exchange high-fives, Liko and Meowscarada also dance, and finally Dot exchanges high-fives with Quaxwell and Tinkatuff before taking back the phone during a group shot. The four Trainers and their Pokémon face the camera. From behind, they look towards the sky, being joined by the Rising Volt Tacklers, [[Ann]], {{an|Nemona}}, and various other Trainers and Pokémon as the camera zooms out. {{j|制作進行}} | * {{r|橋本陸}} | style="{{roundybr|5px}}" lang="ja" | * 橋本陸 |} ===Notes=== ==Trivia== * The scene with a {{p|Krabby}} watching the sunset at the beach is similar to a scene in ''[[EP013|Mystery at the Lighthouse]]''. * This is the first opening theme since the third variant of [[One, Two, Three]] to not show the [[Pokémon|Pocket Monsters]] logo near the beginning. ** This is also the first opening theme that does not show the Pocket Monsters logo at either the beginning or the end; instead, the logo appears between the first chorus and the second stanza, halfway through the animation sequence. * This is the first Japanese opening of {{aniseries|HZ}} where the full version of the song was not released simultaneously on the day it premiered. * The scene near the end of the opening foreshadows [[Character of the day#The Search for Laqua|characters of the day]] who appear in later episodes. * This song and [[Ready Go]] are the first Japanese theme songs not to be published by an imprint of {{wp|Media Factory}} or {{wp|Sony Music Entertainment Japan|Sony Music Japan}} since the ending theme [[Look Look☆Here]]. * This song and [[Ready Go]] are the first Japanese theme songs to be used directly in the English dub of the mainline {{pkmn|animated series}}, with the Japanese version of the song being used for the Asian English release. ** The subtitles in the Asian English release misspell the line "Just me alone" as "Just me along". ==References== {{reflist}} ==Related articles== {{Japanese opening themes}} {{English opening themes}} {{PrevNext |prevlink=Will (song) |prev=Will -Korean ver.- |next=None |list=English opening themes |series=English opening themes (Asia) |colorscheme=ZA}} {{PrevNext |prev=Only One Story |next=Iolite |list=Japanese opening themes |colorscheme=ZA}} {{Project Music notice}} [[Category:Japanese opening themes]] [[es:OPJ28]] [[ja:GET BACK]] [[zh:GET BACK]]
